title: The impact of auditory distraction on retrieval of visual memories
research_question: Does irrelevant auditory information impact objective recollection of visual details during episodic memory retrieval, and does environmental distraction induce domain-general interference that disrupts recollection?

participants.description: Young adults (18-29 years old, 19 males), native speakers of English, healthy, no history of hearing/neurological/psychiatric disease, normal/corrected-to-normal vision. One participant was excluded from the initial N=28.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: 168 target images, each displaying one to four copies of the same object from a three-dimensional perspective, in color, on a plain white background. Objects were common items, controlled for concreteness and namability.

Auditory stimuli presented via sound-canceling headphones: (1) complete silence (headphones off), (2) white noise (flat power spectral density), and (3) ambient sounds recorded at a busy café (restaurant chatter). All auditory stimuli were equated and normalized for power spectral density.

measures.construct: Objective recollection of goal-relevant visual details
measures.instrument: Conditional correct score (proportion of target responses for which individuals correctly recalled the count, given the item was not forgotten)
Proportion of targets in each condition that were given a count (correct or incorrect)
Proportion of lures erroneously given an object count
Verbal exit interview assessing use of visual imagery

mechanisms: Interference between resource-limited, top-down mechanisms that guide the selection of mnemonic details and control processes that mediate interactions with external distractors.
Domain-general interference at a critical locus of top-down cognitive control processes that guide selection of mnemonic details (mnemonic selection).

Capacity-constrained prefrontal cortex (PFC) resources for top-down control may be overwhelmed by processes recruited to resolve interference from irrelevant perceptual information or processes that incidentally mediate attention toward visual distractors.

Interaction between early auditory cortical regions engaged by auditory distractors and regions in the visual association cortex that support visual imagery involved in recollection via cortico-thalamic pathways (bottom-up influence).

tables.description: Behavioral results: Mean performance for 27 participants in three auditory conditions (standard error of the mean) for 168 targets and 36 lures.

limitations: The study's findings regarding the impact of white noise and auditory distraction on episodic retrieval differ from some findings in the irrelevant sound effect (ISE) literature, suggesting task-dependent variations in distraction effects.

The study did not directly examine neural mechanisms of multisensory bottom-up interference or interference with functional networks between sensory regions and PFC sources of domain-general top-down control, which requires future neuroimaging research.
